back_translation: The LORD said to me as follows: 'Go and buy yourself a linen waistcloth and put it on your waist, but do not soak it in water.'
So I bought the waistcloth according to the word of the LORD, and put it on my waist.
Then the word of the LORD came to me a second time, saying:
'Take the waistcloth that you bought and that is on your waist, arise and go to Perath, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock.'
So I went and hid it at Perath, as the LORD commanded me.
After many days had passed, the LORD said to me, 'Arise, go to Perath, and bring back the waistcloth that I commanded you to hide there.'
So I went to Perath, dug it up, and took the waistcloth from the place where I had hidden it. But behold, the waistcloth was ruined—good for nothing at all.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
'Thus says the LORD: In this same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart and have gone after other gods to serve and bow down to them, they will be like this waistcloth that is good for nothing at all.

For as a waistcloth clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me, declares the LORD, that they might be my people, a name, a praise, and a glory; but they would not listen.
You shall speak to them this word: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Every jar shall be filled with wine.' And when they reply to you, 'Do we not know that every jar is filled with wine?'

Then you shall say to them: Thus says the LORD: 'Behold, I will make all the inhabitants of this land drunk—the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem.'
I will dash them against one another, fathers and sons together, declares the LORD. I will not pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, but will destroy them.
Listen and give ear; do not be arrogant, for the LORD has spoken.

Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings darkness, and before your feet stumble on the mountains at twilight, while you hope for light, but he turns it into deep darkness and makes it thick gloom.
But if you will not listen, my soul will weep in secret because of your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly and overflow with tears, because the flock of the LORD has been taken captive.
Say to the king and the queen mother: 'Humble yourselves and take a low seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.'
The cities of the Negev are shut tight, and no one can open them. All Judah has been carried into exile, carried wholly into exile.
Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock given to you, your beautiful flock?
What will you say when he sets over you, as head, those whom you yourself trained to be your close allies? Will not pangs seize you like a woman in labor?
And if you say in your heart, 'Why have these things happened to me?'—it is because of the greatness of your iniquity that your skirts have been lifted up and your body has been violated.
Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? If so, then you who are accustomed to doing evil could also do good.
I will scatter them like chaff driven away by the desert wind.
This is your lot, the portion I have measured out to you, declares the LORD, because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.
I myself will lift your skirts up over your face, and your shame will be seen.

Your adulteries, your lustful neighings, and the lewdness of your prostitution on the hills in the field—I have seen your detestable things. Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long yet until you will be made clean?
